solution: To put decimals in order, line them up vertically so the decimal points stack right on top of each other. $\\[1em]$ Tip: find the number with the most digits after the decimal point. Fill in the empty spaces of the other numbers with placeholder zeros so they are all the same length. This keeps your columns neat. $\\[1em]$ Lined up with matching decimal places: $\\[1em]$ $20.20$ $\\[1em]$ $79.54$ $\\[1em]$ $ 6.32$ $\\[1em]$ $33.74$

Compare the numbers digit by digit, working left to right. $\\[1em]$ Start with the whole-number parts (the digits to the left of the decimal point). If those are different, the bigger whole part wins right away. $\\[1em]$ If two numbers share the same whole-number part, move one digit to the right and compare the tenths. If those are tied too, compare the hundredths, and so on. $\\[1em]$ Here are the whole-number parts: $\\[1em]$ $20.2$ whole-number part is $20$ $\\[1em]$ $79.54$ whole-number part is $79$ $\\[1em]$ $6.32$ whole-number part is $6$ $\\[1em]$ $33.74$ whole-number part is $33$
